question: A steady current flows through a metallic conductor of non-uniform cross-section. How does the drift velocity ($v_d$) of the free electrons change as they move from a wider cross-section to a narrower cross-section?

options.A: It remains constant because current is constant.
options.C: It increases because drift velocity is inversely proportional to the area of cross-section.
options.D: It decreases because drift velocity is directly proportional to the area of cross-section.
